subject: Acoustic guitar and tambourine
observations: The replacement has a rounded acoustic-instrument body with a clear waist, asymmetric perspective, soundhole, wooden bridge and a slanted neck. These curves and the diagonal pose resolve the previous blocky, static appearance.

Broad coral-red and golden-yellow body sections, turquoise headstock/side, warm orange-brown neck, green tambourine and purple ribbons create lively meaningful colour variety. Shading and thin string lines are not counted as extra colour regions.

The soundhole, bridge and strings align coherently along the neck. Four schematic strings and four tuning keys are depicted; this is a simplified four-string acoustic-instrument treatment rather than a literal six-string guitar, but remains recognizable and visually coherent for the child-friendly source.

The green tambourine has a continuous rounded frame and repeated gold jingles; two purple ribbon tails add movement and substantial contrasting shapes. No faces appear on either instrument or the ribbons.
The complete instruments have clear white-space separation and remain within the canvas. Source quality does not require wider rings or any processing-radius threshold.
